partner_result_applied.scope: Noncentral Gaussian three-mode density envelope: covariance >= v I gives density sup <= 1/(2sqrt(2)v).

mathematical_delta.headline: Critical finite rare-fragment non-Lindeberg banks converge to Gaussian plus finite compound-Poisson shifts, whose quadratic-form density remains capped by 3sqrt(2).
mathematical_delta.construction: Each cap-one physical density is an indicator of a central interval of length 1-alpha/m plus finitely many intervals of length alpha_r/m centered at b_r sqrt(m); A_m=diag(J_m/m,J_m/m,-J_m/m).
mathematical_delta.limit: S_j,m => N(0,1/12)+sum_r b_jr Poisson(alpha_jr), independently across banks.
mathematical_delta.non_lindeberg: A rare fragment (alpha,b) contributes exactly alpha*b^2+alpha^3/(12m^3) to the row Lindeberg sum.
mathematical_delta.ceiling: Conditioning on the compound-Poisson shifts and applying the partner theorem gives ||p_Qinfty||_infinity <= 3sqrt(2).
mathematical_delta.exact_negative_fragment_saddle: p_Qinfty(0)=3sqrt(2)e^-alpha sum_k alpha^k/k! exp(-3b^2k^2), strictly below 3sqrt(2) for alpha>0,b!=0.

correction_status: No refuted intermediate is used. The finite-fragment theorem is not an extremality reduction for arbitrary marginals.
unresolved_implication: A witness above 3sqrt(2), if it exists, must escape finite compound-Poisson mesoscopic shifts; finite transient spikes, growing fragment alphabets, other scalings and mixed-leverage core/tail interactions remain open.
next_step: Stress growing-fragment and mixed-leverage core-plus-diffuse-tail product sources for a target-valid peak above 3sqrt(2), or prove a product-preserving ceiling for that branch.
